candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: All right, here is the new $300 contract, with milestones organized by scene. I uploaded a revised script to the shared google folder; it contains only a few minor changes from the previous version. You can skip the text cards because I can handle those myself, so there may be some money left over for fine-tuning, but we’ll see how things progress. Please let me know if anything is unclear. Thanks!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Please make every effort to maintain the correct style as well. The style seems capable of gradually drifting or changing, and it is very important to me that the artistic style be perfect.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: The final video should be entirely in color. Storyboards are frequently black and white as a cost-saving measure.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: I do want the opening aerial establishing shot, but it is a lower priority. We can hold off on it until we have confirmed that everything else we need is completed before using time on that shot.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Would it be worthwhile to generate new set images as the starting frames so that the sets are higher quality? I’m fine with doing that if it would be beneficial. I didn’t realize we would be limited to the resolution of my set images, and I don’t believe their quality is high enough.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: If possible, I would like to retain the long, wide shots at the start of the sequence. I’m okay with creating new sets, provided they match the intended style and remain consistent from shot to shot.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: The first set is wide, the second set is mid, and the third set is closer.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Sorry, my wording was probably confusing because I used "set" in different ways. There are three PAIRS of images, and every pair contains 1 shot of Q and 1 shot of Deadwax. The first two images are long/wide shots, the second two are mid shots, and the third pair consists of closer shots from the waist up.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Ok, these are looking good. There are just a few minor issues left: I can now see the bridge behind Q around his waist, which is poorly placed. Could you remove that bridge as well as the one directly above his head? In the Q images, please keep only the upper bridge so the lower ones aren’t in the way. These images are also missing the character shadows—could you restore those without changing anything else? Thanks for continuing to work through this!

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Ok, one issue I’m running into is that I can’t create the angles I want for these shots. The desired angles were already specified in the script, and the script also noted that the storyboard angle was incorrect. However, if you were working only from the storyboard reel rather than the script, then we were misunderstanding each other. If I’m unable to create the angle I want, add it to the storyboard reel, and show it to you that way, what workflow would be effective for you? How should I communicate the desired angle so you can render the shot accurately?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Another difficulty I’ve had is maintaining the character details I prefer within the style I want. If I provide two images—one showing the desired character details and another showing the intended style—could you try generating an image that combines both?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Also, just to be clear: although I mentioned making a digital comic book with still frames, I’d like to attempt the animation first. I’ll fall back to the digital comic book with still frames only if the animation doesn’t give good results or proves too difficult or expensive.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Ok. Before continuing, I’d like to refine the character style somewhat. It keeps shifting, and I’ve struggled to keep it consistent and precise. Deadwax and Nova are close to what I want, while Q is the furthest away—he looks too clean, simple, and polished. I’m aiming for a rougher graffiti aesthetic. Could you quickly try applying this style to all three characters and send me the results?

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: You can see that it’s rougher and darker, with more sketch-like energy and a stronger attitude.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Out of the three, this one is my favorite in terms of his features and level of detail, if you need a target reference.

candidates.speaker: client
candidates.text: Hi, thank you for following up. The main issue is that it doesn't seem possible to achieve the look I want without investing more, and I may not be able to reach the animation quality I want either. I’d be game if you could help refine the look a little and run a few more animation tests, but I can't justify using up our contract on further look development or additional animation testing when I’m not confident we can achieve the desired result.
